# OutLoud AI collaboration log

**Team 07 · All iterations · Consolidated November 5, 2026**

Record new task prompts, follow-ups and results only in this file, following the [reporting guide](ai-collaboration-guidelines.md). Iteration reports remain separate. Historical iteration labels are retained as recorded; dates do not establish an iteration transition.

## Consolidation and source status

Seven retained source snapshots are consolidated here. The published v8 logs form the historical backbone. Root-only tasks and supplements from the protected local checkout, two pending worktrees and the previously published Wiki log are incorporated below. Exact task headings determine shared task identity; differently titled records remain separate. A source-labelled supplement preserves a differing historical record; it does not supersede confirmed attribution, prove a later fix, or establish new acceptance. Repeated copies of the same task block are omitted. Identical requests in different tasks remain separate interactions.

Published source: [`cdb8055`](https://github.com/snuhcs-course/swpp-2026-project-team-07/commit/cdb8055f0fd5022aafccb47625889d3f9a403f5f). The November 5 consolidation validation records source hashes and per-task preservation outside the application source tree. Earlier per-iteration log paths are compatibility indexes; frozen `docs/history/` records and immutable commit links remain unchanged.

#### I2. Hosted Whisper adapter and response-shape repair, September 29

- **Output and use:** Codex integrated hosted Whisper and generated a Korean TTS sample in PR #3.
- **Error → correction:** The adapter assumed a success response supported `model_dump()`. An independent Codex reviewer found that non-object responses could escape as `AttributeError`; Codex added a type guard and regression cases. This was an implementation defect. Repair time was not recorded.
- **Verification and human role:** The suite passed 23 backend tests; a live TTS call returned 38 words from 23,902 ms. Injoon reported inspecting the restaged changes. Human-speech accuracy and end-to-end app integration were unverified; the repair was AI-written.

[Evidence](https://github.com/snuhcs-course/swpp-2026-project-team-07/pull/3).

<a id="i1-y2-empty-android-timeline-after-stop-october-78"></a>

#### Y2. Empty Android timeline after Stop, October 7–8

- **Error and detection:** Jooyoung reported an empty Android timeline. Code read `durationMillis` after Stop, but Android reset it to zero, causing timeline filtering to discard the events.
- **Correction and outcome:** Codex added `stopCapture.ts` to pause and save native duration before stopping. Jooyoung confirmed the timeline appeared; an independent Codex reviewer checked the staged fix. The implementation defect was repaired by Codex.
- **Evidence and limits:** PR #13 (`040880f`) records 21 tests, Android export and native launch. Quick Stop, re-recording and automated helper coverage were pending at that revision; elapsed repair cost was not recorded.

[Evidence](https://github.com/snuhcs-course/swpp-2026-project-team-07/blob/040880f8a21b2f866228984e9fb3c438fa6ee4bf/docs/ai-use.md#L319-L352).

```text
PLEASE IMPLEMENT THIS PLAN:
# Playback transcript and main-screen tabs

## Summary

Place the scrolling transcript inside the playback card and keep the current word visible during playback. Split the main screen into **Home**, **Presentations**, and **Library**, using the tab roles you selected.

## Playback changes

- Arrange the playback card as: **slide → playback controls → transcript**. Remove the separate transcript card below analysis progress.
- Show the full transcript in a bounded, independently scrolling panel.
- Reuse word timestamps and the player’s existing 100 ms status updates. Highlight the word at the actual audio position; preserve correct behavior for pause, seeking, replay, and silence. [Expo audio reference](https://docs.expo.dev/versions/v57.0.0/sdk/audio/)
- Keep tap-to-seek. Seeking preserves whether audio was playing or paused and updates both the slide and highlighted word.
- Use measured text-line positions to scroll only when the active word leaves the visible panel. Avoid scrolling the whole results screen.
- Manual transcript scrolling pauses automatic following while highlighting continues. Show **Follow playback** to return to the current position and resume following.
- Preserve punctuation, whitespace, and Korean/English text. Show readable text when timestamps cannot be mapped reliably; show distinct waiting and no-speech states.
- Reset transcript scrolling and following state when opening a different attempt. Retain audio playback when slides or transcription are unavailable.

## Main-screen navigation

Use Expo Router’s existing JavaScript tabs inside the root stack, ordered **Home · Presentations · Library**, with Home selected initially. Viewer, recording, playback, and description screens remain full-screen stack destinations. [Expo tabs reference](https://docs.expo.dev/router/advanced/tabs/)

| Tab | Content and actions |
|---|---|
| **Home** | Welcome text, **Import PDF**, **Start practice**, and the three newest saved rehearsals with deck title, date, and status. Import opens the existing picker/viewer flow; Start practice opens Presentations. |
| **Presentations** | Imported decks grouped with their rehearsal history. Each deck opens its slides to start practice; saved attempts open playback and retain upload-retry/recovery access. |
| **Library** | PDF import, saved PDF list, open/remove actions, clearly labelled sample slides, and the existing connection check. Rehearsal history moves to Presentations. |

- Refresh saved data whenever a tab gains focus; reuse existing PDF and attempt storage.
- Keep PDF removal protection for decks with saved rehearsals.
- Provide useful empty states linking to PDF import.
- Add `/presentations` and `/library`; `/` becomes Home. Update existing fallback buttons to the appropriate destination.
- Preserve Back navigation, recording exit protection, and pausing playback when leaving review.

## Verification

- Existing playback baseline: **10 tests passed**.
- Extend tests for transcript-to-line mapping, repeated words, punctuation, Korean/English text, silence, backward seeking, and scroll-follow state.
- Verify recent-attempt ordering and grouping by deck, including empty data.
- Run `npm run check` and `npm run bundle:android` from the mobile project.
- On Android, verify long-transcript following, manual scrolling and resumption, word seeking, replay, tab navigation, import cancellation, upload retry, and recording exit protection.
- Check narrow screens and enlarged text for clipping and nested-scroll problems.

## Assumptions and handoff

- Continue the existing mobile-flow work while preserving the staged playback-slide changes and unrelated files.
- Reuse current styling and installed dependencies. Backend APIs, transcript wire types, and stored-data formats remain unchanged.
- Record changes and actual verification in the README and AI-use log. Commit and push remain subject to the repository’s review and user-inspection workflow.
```

**Approved AI plan**

```text
PLEASE IMPLEMENT THIS PLAN:
# Simplify OutLoud around practice and review

## Summary

Use **Home + Presentations** as the two main tabs. Home prioritizes practicing your latest deck; saved rehearsals open **Feedback first**, with Playback one tap away. Keep the blue accent and reduce repeated headings, bordered cards, explanatory text, and large secondary buttons.

## Screen changes

- **Home:** Replace the large introduction with “Practice again,” the deck title, and one primary button. Choose the most recently practiced available deck, falling back to the newest imported PDF. Show “Choose another” and three recent rehearsals as compact tappable rows. With no decks, make “Import PDF” the primary action.
- **Presentations:** Merge Library into this screen. Show one row per deck with its title and rehearsal count; keep Import in the header. Tapping a deck opens its slides shortcut and rehearsal history. Put PDF removal in an overflow menu, retaining the existing protection for PDFs with recordings. Preserve access to rehearsals whose PDF is unavailable.
- **Settings:** Move backend connection information and the clearly labelled sample preview here, accessible from Home’s header.
- **Slide setup and recording:** Put optional audience input behind “Audience.” Keep limits and save-on-exit behavior concise and visible before recording. During recording, prioritize the slide, page controls, timer, and Start/Stop action. Keep recording controls visible without scrolling at normal text size.
- **Review:** Add **Feedback / Playback** tabs within the rehearsal screen. Feedback shows available suggestions with expandable evidence, followed by collapsed “Timing & pace.” Pending, disabled, or unavailable feedback gets a short truthful message and a Playback shortcut. Playback contains the slide, compact audio controls, and synchronized transcript; the full slide-visit list is expandable.
- **Status and errors:** Replace the expanded processing card with a short status and expandable “Analysis details.” Keep actionable failures, recovery, and valid retry actions visible. Selecting suggestion evidence opens Playback and seeks to that moment.

## Implementation boundaries

- Use simple rows and dividers, one title per screen, and one dominant action per view. Retain readable text and at least 48-dp action targets.
- Add presentation-detail navigation keyed by the existing local deck ID and a Settings route. Redirect `/library` to Presentations and update internal links.
- Keep the audio player above the Review tab content so switching tabs preserves position and play/pause state. Evidence seeking also preserves that state.
- Reuse existing storage, upload, recovery, and processing behavior. No backend API changes, storage migrations, new dependencies, or overall presentation score.
- Preserve current staged work. Update README navigation guidance and task-level AI-use evidence with implementation and verification results.

## Verification

- Run `npm run check` and `npm run bundle:android` from `mobile/`.
- Test latest-deck selection, empty catalogs, duplicate titles, unavailable PDFs, and retained rehearsal history.
- Check Android navigation, long titles, large text, and small screens; ensure recording controls remain reachable.
- Verify Feedback-first behavior while processing, disabled, failed, and complete; confirm recovery and retry remain accessible.
- Recheck transcript seeking, evidence seeking, repeated/backward slide visits, tab switching during playback, and saving when leaving a recording.

Acceptance: normal browsing shows compact lists; each screen has one clear next action; technical details appear on demand without hiding failures or removing existing capabilities.
```

**Approved AI plan (excerpt)**

```text
PLEASE IMPLEMENT THIS PLAN:
# Recording Storage, Then Whisper API

## Goals and sequence

1. Finish, validate, and publish the existing storage implementation as **`feature/recording-storage-upload`**.
2. Report what works, remaining limitations, and the next implementation scope. **Stop for your confirmation.**
3. After confirmation, implement **`feature/whisper-api-processing`** using the local multi-agent pipeline.

Transcription will use **OpenAI’s hosted Whisper API (`whisper-1`)**. No local Whisper inference or model downloads will be introduced.

## First implementation: finish recording storage

The current storage changes exist locally but remain uncommitted and independently unreviewed.

- Rename `feature/attempt-processing` to `feature/recording-storage-upload`.
- Finish SQLite recording checkpoints, restart recovery, local/server deck mapping, retryable uploads, and server file persistence.
- Verify that retries preserve the recording UUID, identical submissions deduplicate, and conflicting submissions return an explicit error.
- Keep uploaded recordings visibly **awaiting analysis**. Storage completion must not imply successful transcription.
- Preserve the existing limits: 10 slides, 20 MiB PDF, 10-minute recordings, and **25,000,000 audio bytes**.
- Correct stale documentation and assess dependency advisories introduced by this change.

**Acceptance:** record a real PDF rehearsal, restart the app, replay saved audio, attempt an offline upload, reconnect and retry, then restart the server and retrieve the same saved recording.

Publish one storage PR, based on `feature/pdf-recording` while that dependency remains unmerged. Do not merge either PR.

## Local multi-agent methodology

Use the existing runner at `tools/agents/pipeline.py` in the local pipeline worktree. Its workflow is:

**Planner → parallel mobile/backend investigators → one implementation agent → checks → independent reviewer → bounded repair/review → inspection**

- Run its preflight and tests before relying on it. Use the configured Codex model without overriding it.
- Give each run a bounded task, acceptance criteria, prototype references, and explicit exclusions. Only investigators run concurrently; one agent owns code changes and shared contracts.
- For storage, export the existing changes—including new files—as a frozen patch against their exact base. The pipeline implementation agent imports that patch into its isolated worktree before making confirmed fixes. Preserve the original worktree.
- Transfer the reviewed result back to the named feature branch, verify that its staged content matches the reviewed/tested patch, and record evidence in `docs/ai-use.md`.
- Keep pipeline-generated branches internal. Publish only the requested `feature/*` branches.
- The runner stops before commits and publication. The coordinating agent handles the authorized PR workflow and reports human review as pending.

The pipeline does not replace Android, PostgreSQL, Redis/Celery, or live-provider checks.
```

<a id="i1-a7-diagnose-and-fix-intermittent-scaffold-checks-october-11"></a>

#### A7. Diagnose and fix intermittent Scaffold checks, October 11

**Contributor:** Injoon · **Date:** 2026-10-11 · **Tool:** OpenAI Codex · **Model:** not recorded

```text
what are scaffold checks and why did they fail
```

```text
How do we fix this
```

- **Investigation and correction:** Codex's prior “all checks passed” summary described passing pre-merge PR checks too broadly. Post-merge main runs 38109256014 and 38109391886 failed mobile tests despite passing backend checks. Logs showed a Library cancellation assertion and an absent PDF validator. The initial inference that these were only test timing problems was incomplete: delayed I/O also exposed an application race.
- **Cause and changes:** The Library test assumed one event-loop turn completed real catalog I/O and could inspect the preceding request instead of a new refresh. Tests now wait for bounded, observable prerequisites without replaying actions or relaxing cancellation assertions. Empty PDF catalog discovery also replaced the initial shared empty array, restarting the media session and cancelling an in-progress PDF download. `useReviewPdf` now reuses the same empty candidate array; populated candidates and identity changes still use the existing logic. A regression checks reference stability after asynchronous discovery, and the detached-renderer test still verifies stale failures cannot erase a replacement.
- **Reproduction:** A temporary Node preload delayed filesystem `stat` and stream-reader `read` by 25 ms. The original two tests failed; after test waits alone the PDF case still timed out. The new empty-catalog regression failed before the source fix. With both fixes, all three targeted tests passed under delayed I/O. No test is skipped and no production timeout is increased.
- **Environment:** Initial full typecheck found the investigation clone still had PR #17 dependencies installed (missing expo-crypto/expo-sqlite). Codex installed the current lockfile before final checks; no dependency files were changed. Final Node 24 verification passed TypeScript, lint, all 289 mobile tests and Android export. Twenty delayed-I/O runs passed all three targeted cases (60 executions). Independent Codex review found no actionable defects and separately passed the same three delayed cases on Node 26. Source, tests and dependencies outside the five-file fix are unchanged. The fix PR records publication and CI results. No new native-device, live-provider or human review is claimed.

**Contributor:** Seoyeon · **Tool:** OpenAI Codex · **Model:** GPT-6 (exact identifier not recorded)

- **Actual pasted request (verbatim):**

```text
# OutLoud Iteration 2 — Improve AI Cues: Must Cover & Go Deeper

## Objective

Revise the existing Phase 2 AI cue system to provide two distinct categories of presentation guidance:

1. **Must Cover:** Essential explanations that the presenter should communicate for the audience to understand the current slide.
2. **Go Deeper:** Optional additional explanations that enrich the presentation beyond what is explicitly shown on the slide.

The current implementation often generates cues that merely restate slide content. The objective is to make AI cues genuinely useful for preparing what to say, not simply summarizing the presentation.

Implement this as a focused Phase 2 improvement. Do not advance to Phase 3.

## 1. Must Cover — Essential explanations

**Definition:** The minimum essential information that a presenter should verbally communicate for the audience to understand the slide's main message.

Requirements:

- Generate 0–3 Must Cover points per slide.
- Every point must be directly grounded in the current slide's text, charts, diagrams, or other visual evidence.
- Focus on understanding and interpretation, not simply repeating the visible content.
- Prioritize the main argument, essential comparisons, numerical interpretations, and conclusions.
- Do not generate a cue for every bullet point.
- Avoid generic instructions such as "Explain this slide."
- Do not invent missing facts or interpretations.
- A slide may have zero Must Cover points if no meaningful verbal explanation is necessary.

Example:

Slide: Accuracy increased from 80% to 92%.

Bad:
- "Accuracy increased from 80% to 92%."
- "The model has higher accuracy."

Good:
- "Clarify that the improvement is 12 percentage points, rather than a 12% relative improvement."
- "Explain what the comparison establishes about the proposed model."

Must Cover points should express essential speaking objectives rather than a script the presenter must repeat word for word.

## 2. Go Deeper — Additional enriching explanations

**Definition:** Optional explanations, insights, connections, or perspectives that could make the presentation more informative, convincing, or engaging.

Requirements:

- Generate 0–3 Go Deeper suggestions per slide.
- Use the full presentation as context, not only the current slide.
- Suggestions may go beyond information explicitly written on the slide.
- Identify opportunities to explain reasoning, implications, background, limitations, practical examples, or relationships between slides.
- Prioritize insights that add meaningful value beyond reading the slide.
- Make suggestions specific to the presentation's actual content.
- Avoid repeating Must Cover points.
- Avoid generic advice such as "Provide more details" or "Discuss implications."
- Do not fabricate external facts, causal explanations, experimental results, or research findings.
- If a useful explanation requires information that is unavailable, frame it as a question or suggestion for the presenter to investigate or clarify.
- Generate fewer suggestions when a slide does not offer meaningful opportunities for enrichment.

Example:

Slide: Accuracy increased from 80% to 92%.

Good:
- "Discuss which model changes contributed to the improvement, if supported by your experiments."
- "Explain whether this accuracy improvement has meaningful practical consequences."
- "Connect this improvement to the limitations of the baseline discussed earlier."

The additional points are optional and must not automatically be treated as missing explanations during post-rehearsal feedback.

## 3. Grounding and source references

Preserve the evidence-grounding guarantees from Phase 2, while supporting the different requirements of both categories.

**Must Cover:**
- Must reference supported facts from the current slide.
- Must not rely on uncertain visual evidence for factual claims.
- Must not introduce unsupported conclusions.

**Go Deeper:**
- May reference the current slide or other slides in the same deck.
- Should retain appropriate source references for factual premises.
- May suggest questions or explanatory opportunities whose answers aren't present in the slides.
- Must distinguish supported statements from questions requiring additional information.
- Must not present unsupported explanations as established facts.

Inspect the existing evidence-reference format and extend it as necessary for cross-slide grounding.

Do not weaken validation simply to accommodate more creative suggestions.

## 4. Backend and schema changes

Extend the existing immutable slide-profile system.

Requirements:

- Introduce separate structured collections for `must_cover` and `go_deeper`.
- Each collection supports 0–3 items.
- Preserve slide identity, source identity, extracted facts, uncertainty, and other existing profile fields.
- Use a new prompt version and schema version so historical cached outputs aren't silently treated as equivalent.
- Preserve existing historical profile/description schemas and their compatibility.
- Reuse existing `DescriptionSet` persistence, jobs, quotas, provider receipts, retry handling, and Celery recovery.
- Do not create another independent AI-job infrastructure.
- Do not rescan slides unnecessarily when the current profile scope is already valid.
- Ensure the full-deck context needed by Go Deeper is available to generation.
- Invalidate and regenerate profiles when relevant slide content, prompt, schema, or model identity changes.
- Prevent duplicate generation for the same scope.

Inspect the existing architecture before determining the exact schema changes.

Document any API changes in `docs/api-contract.md`.

## 5. Frontend UI changes

Reuse JJ's existing Rehearse screen and Cues control.

Within the existing cue area, distinguish the two categories:

**Must Cover**
- Clearly labeled as essential speaking points.
- Presented as concise, readable guidance.

**Go Deeper**
- Clearly labeled as optional suggestions.
- Visually distinguishable from Must Cover.
- Focused on enriching the presentation rather than repeating its main content.

Choose a compact interaction that fits JJ's existing design language. A two-category toggle or segmented control within the existing cue area is acceptable.

Do not add a standalone screen or unrelated UI redesign.

Retain:
- Scrolling for longer content.
- Offline caching.
- Explicit pending, failed, uncertain, stale, and unavailable states.
- Existing retry behavior.
- Slide navigation.
- Selected-run and recording behavior.

Ensure empty categories are handled naturally without placeholder or fabricated cues.

## 6. Future feedback compatibility

Design the categories so Phase 5 can eventually evaluate them differently.

**Must Cover:**
May inform future content-coverage analysis, but missing a cue must not automatically count as a presentation problem.

Future analysis should consider paraphrasing, audience context, adjacent-slide explanations, and whether the essential meaning was actually communicated.

**Go Deeper:**
Should inform optional improvement suggestions rather than mandatory coverage requirements.

Do not implement Phase 5 feedback behavior now. Only preserve the information needed for it.

## 7. Evaluation and testing

Add automated tests for:

- Slides with many bullet points.
- Image-only graphs.
- Numerical comparisons.
- Sparse title and closing slides.
- Ambiguous or unreadable graphs.
- Slides with no worthwhile additional suggestions.
- Connections between multiple slides.
- Unsupported causal explanations.
- Duplicate or redundant cues.
- Category boundaries of 0–3 items.
- Unsupported source references.
- Cache invalidation following schema/prompt changes.
- Historical profile compatibility.
- Duplicate job admission and stale responses.
- Offline caching and reopening.
- Correct category display and navigation.

Also evaluate cue quality using representative presentation slides.

Compare the original Phase 2 cue behavior against the revised categories using the same input slides.

Evaluate:
1. **Specificity:** Is the suggestion relevant to this particular slide?
2. **Non-redundancy:** Does it provide more than a paraphrase of visible text?
3. **Usefulness:** Would this help someone prepare what to say?
4. **Grounding:** Are factual premises supported?
5. **Category correctness:** Is it appropriately classified as Must Cover or Go Deeper?

Do not claim real-model quality is verified based only on mocked provider outputs. If live-provider testing is unavailable, report that limitation explicitly.

## 8. Verification and handoff

- Run `mobile/npm run check`.
- Run `mobile/npm run bundle:android`.
- Run backend checks and tests with `config.test_settings`.
- Check migrations and ensure historical data remains compatible.
- Verify new worker behavior with PostgreSQL/Redis where appropriate.
- Test the updated cue interface on Android.
- Obtain an independent review of the staged implementation.
- Fix confirmed issues and rerun affected tests.
- Record AI-use and actual verification evidence.

Preserve unrelated changes.

Stage only the intended modifications and present the exact staged diff, verification results, quality-evaluation evidence, and unresolved limitations for inspection.

**Do not commit, push, merge, implement Phase 3, or modify the held presentation requirements sheet without explicit authorization.**

## Success criterion

After this change, OutLoud should no longer behave like an AI slide summarizer.

The Must Cover category should help presenters identify **what they need to communicate for the slide to be understood**.

The Go Deeper category should help presenters discover **what additional explanations could make the presentation stronger**.

Both categories must be specific, useful, non-redundant, and appropriately grounded in the presentation.
```

Existing in-panel compact selector and scrolling; no analysis/recording/requirements changes.
- **Execution plan:** (1) Red/green schema/prompt/reference/history tests; (2) version-aware mobile validation/cache/status and category selector with renderer interactions; (3) full mobile/backend/PostgreSQL checks and real receipt/job recovery; (4) same-slide live v1/v2 evaluation and Android checks; (5) stage only intended changes, independent review, repairs/retests, exact diff/evidence handoff.
- **Limits:** Source references prove supported premises, not arbitrary natural-language semantic truth. Real-model evaluation assesses specificity, redundancy, usefulness, grounding and category correctness; mocks alone do not prove quality.

<a id="i2-theme-toggle-half-turn-correction-october-15-2026"></a>

### Theme toggle half-turn correction, October 15, 2026

**Contributor:** Jaewon Choi (requester) · **Tool:** OpenAI Codex · **Model:** not recorded

#### Prompt — verbatim

```text
the icon doesnt rotate 180 so the horizontal axis keeps moving at an angle
```

The requester clarified which icon after an agent question:

```text
the dark mode light mode
```

#### AI-generated and retained work

- Found that the sun/moon toggle computed its next animation target from the current animated value. A second tap during the 560 ms spin could therefore finish at a fractional turn and leave the light/dark split tilted. The toggle now tracks whole half-turn targets separately from the animated value, so each completed transition ends on a 180-degree alignment. The theme choice and stored preference continue to work as before.

#### Verification and limits

- Agent-operated TypeScript typecheck and uncached ESLint passed. The offline Android release APK built, installed and launched on the connected Samsung phone. Source inspection confirmed that each mode change targets the next integer half-turn, including when a previous animation is still moving.
- On the phone, two quick taps left the icon's split level in dark mode; a separate tap left it level in light mode. Codex restored dark mode afterward. The screenshots show settled endpoints, not every animation frame. No app test suite, separate AI reviewer, human test, commit or push was performed for this correction.

```text
PLEASE IMPLEMENT THIS PLAN:
# Permanent Cues panel with Play preserved

## Recording layout

- Replace the normal recording screen’s transcript body with a permanent panel titled **Cues**, using Nakajima’s existing placement, typography, spacing and theme.

## Verification

- Cover visibility before/during recording; forward/backward navigation; revisits; reopening; recovery; rotation; both themes; long cues; and missing/stale/failure/retry states.
- Assert no generation requests occur from navigation, theme changes, rotation or reopening.
```

````text
## Where each capability belongs

| Capability | Current integration | Intended placement |
|---|---|---|
| Time and audience requirements | Local setup and AI context disagree | Existing setup overlay, reused for editing |
| Must Cover / Go Deeper | Permanent recording panel implemented | Keep in normal recording layout beside Play |
| Selected-slide AI feedback | Retained but buried | Main content of Review |
| AI status and finding counts | Disconnected from prominent indicators | Shared indicators across Review, Full Review and Home |
| Transcript corrections and word playback | Retained in recording-details sheet | Review → **Transcript & corrections** |
| Finding evidence | Retained through playback sheet | Expandable finding details → existing evidence playback |
| Run transcripts and playback | Retained | Full Review |
| Audience questions, answers and history | Retained; entry requires gesture | Existing Q&A screen, with tappable Review entry |
| Older recording-wide coaching and descriptions | Retained alongside newer feedback | Clearly labelled, collapsed recording tools |
| Take comparison | Retained | Existing Compare; preserve Keep current / Overwrite |

## Implementation changes

### 1. Connect presentation setup to authoritative requirements

- Reuse the existing setup overlay after import and from an **Edit time & audience** action in the idle recording header. Stop playback while editing; disable opening during countdown or capture.
- Save through the existing revisioned context client. Initialize new imports to five minutes and General audience; existing presentations load their saved values.
- Support 1–30 minutes. Preserve existing exact durations until the user moves the slider; slider interaction uses 30-second increments.
- Keep audience presets, add **Other…** within the overlay for existing/custom values, and respect the existing 500-code-point validation. Allow explicitly clearing audience or duration.
- Persist confirmed offline choices separately from server-accepted requirements. Unsaved edits disappear on cancellation; confirmed pending choices survive reopening.
- Serialize default initialization and user saves through one writer. Defaults must never overwrite confirmed choices.
- Resolve lost acknowledgements through GET. Preserve conflicting local/server values and offer **Use server** or **Keep mine**, with revision checking.
- Show **Saved on phone · sync pending**, failure and conflict states. Pending changes immediately mark dependent feedback/Q&A outdated and block generation until synchronized.
- Restore default, required and suggested timing labels. Changing requirements must preserve valid slide-only cue profiles.

### 2. Share one source of AI status

Extract the existing validated cache, scope and freshness handling into a shared feedback reader used by Review, Full Review and Home.

- Preserve existing cache keys and exact selected attempt/slide/segment identities, including repeated visits.
- Read existing singleton slide scopes separately; combining slides would address a different backend analysis.
- Reuse current transcript, correction and requirement revision checks. Pending/conflicting corrections must invalidate displayed feedback immediately.
- Expose current status and verified finding counts; do not manufacture percentage grades.
- Distinguish successful, partial, insufficient evidence, invalid evidence, failed, unavailable, analyzing, outdated and not analyzed.
- Only successful current results with zero findings may show **No issues found**. Partial or unavailable results must never appear clean.
- Share and deduplicate GET requests, with at most three concurrent requests and one polling timer for active jobs. Stop polling covered screens.
- Keep provider admission in the existing initial-generation hosts and explicit update/retry actions.

### 3. Make Review the primary feedback interface

Preserve Nakajima’s typography, theme, ring, timing bars, slide preview and playback styling.

Use one page-level scroll in this order:

1. Selected-slide AI status ring and verified finding count.
2. Timing/filler metrics and slide navigation.
3. Slide preview and saved-audio playback.
4. **AI feedback**: up to four prioritized findings, with observation, advice and expandable evidence.
5. Optional **Go deeper** enrichment, visibly separate from problems.
6. **Transcript & corrections**, Full Review and Audience Q&A actions.

Replace the small nested feedback scroll. Keep Refresh, Update feedback, dependency recovery and uncertain-retry confirmation beside the relevant state.

The recording screen’s Review button should open the currently selected slide. After finishing a recording, retain the existing automatic choice of an initial review slide.

### 4. Connect Full Review and Home

- Replace Strong/Good/Needs work/Weak tiles with the shared AI statuses and finding counts.
- Full Review shows assessed slides, slides with findings, partial results, pending work, outdated results and recovery states.
- Its ring shows **N of M recorded slides assessed**, explicitly representing completion rather than presentation quality.
- Home uses the same compact assessment summary and continues opening Full Review.
- Keep duration, fillers and pace separately labelled as measured metrics.
- Preserve Full Review’s transcript and run/slide playback. Disclose missing source audio before playing a partial run.
- Selecting a tile opens that slide’s Review; corrections remain accessible from there.

### 5. Preserve supporting workflows

- Keep permanent Cues and Play unchanged, including rotation, recovery, caching and slide synchronization.
- Retain correction suggestions, confirmation, restore, synchronization, conflicts, original-word playback and source ownership.
- Evidence playback shows the selected quote and source interval and plays that bounded interval through existing playback controls.
- Label older coaching **Recording-wide suggestions** under collapsed recording tools; do not mix it into current selected-slide counts.
- Restore tappable Q&A/back actions while retaining gestures.
- Replace obsolete “requirements entry unavailable” messages with an action opening the shared setup overlay.
- Preserve Q&A preparation, explicit updates, saved generations, follow-ups, answer recording/transcription and retry identity.
- Keep Compare’s selection mechanics and measured comparisons; do not add a new AI comparison system.

## Verification and handoff

- Test setup synchronization, defaults races, offline reopening, lost acknowledgements, conflicts, concurrent edits, API isolation and duration/audience boundaries.
- Test consistent indicators across all three screens, including zero/four findings, partial, failed, insufficient, outdated and unavailable states.
- Assert navigation, reopening, theme, rotation, overview refresh and settings operations do not admit provider generation.
- Retain repeated/backward-visit, correction → stale feedback → explicit update → evidence playback tests.
- Verify long findings, both themes, larger text, scrolling and tappable accessibility routes.
- Run mobile `npm run check` and `npm run bundle:android`.
- On the physical phone, verify the integration checkout and backend readiness, then exercise setup, cues, recording, Review, corrections, evidence, Full Review and Q&A. Report actual device results separately from mocked tests and real-provider checks.
- Update `docs/ai-use.md` and the existing verification record. Stage intended changes, obtain independent review, fix/retest findings, and present the exact staged result for final inspection before any commit.

## Boundaries

Continue on `it2/integration-ai-nakajima`. Reuse existing backend contracts, prompts, generation scope and native dependencies. Add no standalone AI screen or historical-recording browser. Preserve saved media and caches. This plan incorporates your choices: authoritative AI status, connected setup and findings directly in Review.
````

````text
\<proposed_plan> # Plan &#x20;

Make review navigation follow the recording sequence and make Full Review easy to find from slide review.

## Scope

- First saved recording per presentation: **Stop and Review → Full Review**, including recordings stopped early.
- After another recording: **Stop and Review → the relevant slide’s review**.
- Keep recording storage, AI processing and backend contracts unchanged.

## Action items

- Use the existing per-presentation saved-take counter for one shared routing rule. Reopening Review does not change the destination; keeping an older take does not reset the counter.
- Apply that rule after saving, when tapping Review, and when recovering an interrupted recording. Navigate without waiting for AI analysis.
- Preserve retake comparison: show Keep/Overwrite when required, then open the relevant slide review after confirmation. Cancel/Back keeps the existing recording and returns to rehearsal.
- Move **Full Review** into a prominent, fixed action below the slide-review title, outside the scrolling transcript and feedback. Use the existing theme, review icon and an accessible touch target; remove the buried duplicate.
- Preserve return navigation and slide selection: Full Review opened from rehearsal returns there; Full Review opened from slide review returns to that slide. Stop playback when switching.
- Add tests for first and subsequent recordings, partial recordings, reopening/restarting, Keep/Overwrite, rejected retakes, and whole-presentation redos.
- Verify the Full Review action stays visible with long transcripts and feedback. Run `npm run check`, `npm run bundle:android`, and Android navigation checks; record results and obtain independent review.

## Defaults

“First” means the first saved recording for that presentation, regardless of slide coverage. Later whole-presentation redos also follow the subsequent-recording rule. Preserve existing local documentation edits; commit and push remain separate actions.\
\</proposed_plan>
````

```text
# Integrate our OutLoud app with Scribe-only transcription

## Summary

Deliver **our complete `codex/presentation-score` implementation with ElevenLabs Scribe v2 replacing Whisper exclusively**. Normalize transcription at the provider boundary so existing scoring, feedback, corrections, Q&A, playback, and navigation continue using their current contracts.

Use **`integration/ai-feedback-with-scribe`** consistently for the integration branch, push, and PR, as confirmed.

## 1. Branch integration and preservation

- Refresh `origin/main` and record both source revisions. Verify our branch contains the intended scoring, Step 1, navigation, layout, cue, and feedback reliability work before merging. Inspect staged, unstaged, and untracked source for missing dependencies; report any required unfinished work before including it.
- Create the isolated integration branch from `origin/main`, then merge `codex/presentation-score` into it, retaining both histories.
- Resolve application conflicts using our implementation. Retain main’s Scribe functionality and adapt it to our application rather than importing main’s older screens or workflows.
- Compare the integrated tree against our baseline. Establish a transcription compatibility allowlist; application source outside it must remain unchanged.
- Preserve existing worktrees, staging backups, unrelated changes, and historical migration files. Do not restore discontinued Step 2 or scoring experiments.

## 2. Scribe-only transcription boundary

- Use only `elevenlabs / scribe_v2`, configured through backend `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, with the existing HTTPX dependency.
- Remove Whisper request construction, historical receipt decoding, transcription provider selection, and fallback logic. Keep OpenAI dependencies and configuration required by existing feedback, scoring, and Q&A evaluation.
- Retain main’s deterministic vocabulary extraction from visited slides, capped at 100 hints, private submitted-option snapshots, and PDF extracted-text NUL handling.
- Normalize Scribe into the existing `{text, words: [{text, start_ms, end_ms}]}` transcript contract. Preserve recognized fillers, original audio, integer-millisecond timing, existing timestamp validation, and slide alignment.
- Preserve no-speech gating, repeated and zero-duration visits, saved Scribe transcript reuse, duplicate prevention, interruption recovery, cooldowns, and explicit uncertain-charge recovery. Make no automatic provider retries.
- Restrict public transcription provenance validation to the Scribe identity, retaining the existing null provenance states before a provider request. Reject unsupported identities without introducing Whisper compatibility paths.

## 3. Database and consent

- Preserve main’s `0007_provider_request_options` and our migration chain through `0010_slide_review_membership`.
- Add one minimal merge migration joining those histories. Set transcription request defaults to Scribe through additive migration-state changes; do not rewrite committed migrations or migrate historical transcripts.
- Verify one valid migration leaf and reliable fresh initialization. Do not reset development data, migrate shared databases, or add historical upgrade/recovery work.
- Use fresh Scribe-specific consent covering audio and vocabulary hints derived from visited slides. Do not migrate or accept old OpenAI transcription consent.
- Apply consent checks to our existing recording and durable Q&A transcription entry points. Saved-result reads and status polling remain available without consent.
- In Q&A, Cancel preserves the pending answer; Continue resumes the same answer identity. Keep existing dialogs, styling, retry confirmation, and workflow structure.

## 4. Verification and regression gates

- Test Scribe request construction, visited-slide-only hints, the 100-hint limit, fillers, timestamp normalization, malformed responses, no-speech results, provider failures, duplicate submissions, uncertainty, and worker interruption.
- Verify saved Scribe receipts/transcripts recover without another provider submission; verify no Whisper fallback exists.
- Run existing application regressions for automatic overall/per-slide scoring, rubric arithmetic, singleton feedback, compact context, corrections and staleness, durable Q&A, navigation, recording/playback, evidence links, zero-duration/repeated visits, and saved assessments.
- Run the full backend suite, Django system checks, migration consistency/drift checks, and fresh SQLite/PostgreSQL migration checks using disposable databases.
- Run mobile `npm run check`, Android export, and affected Android emulator flows with mocked inference.
- Use mocked providers throughout. Explicitly document unavailable checks; do not infer device or live-provider success from exports or unit tests.

## 5. Review and PR delivery

- Review the complete diff against our scoring baseline, confirming unchanged application behavior outside the approved transcription compatibility scope.
- Obtain independent code review, fix actionable findings, and rerun affected checks.
- Update API/setup documentation and AI-use evidence, clearly distinguishing current verification from historical results.
- Present the reviewed diff, test results, included dependencies, and remaining limitations for final inspection. **Stop before committing until review approval.**
- After approval, commit intended changes, push `integration/ai-feedback-with-scribe`, and open a PR targeting `main` titled **“Integrate complete OutLoud application with ElevenLabs Scribe v2 transcription.”**
- Do not merge the PR, deploy, alter shared databases, rewrite history, delete worktrees/backups, modify secrets or running services, or make paid provider calls.
```

```text
# Fix #44–46 while preserving the current design

## Constraints
```

#### Prompt — verbatim

```text
**Slide 1 — How OutLoud gives scores users can check**

**Problem:** An AI can give a convincing score without clearly showing why.

**Our solution:**

1. **Connect speech to slides.** Use slide-change times and word timestamps to identify what the speaker said on each slide.
2. **Assess three questions.** Did the speaker cover the important ideas? Explain them sufficiently? Speak clearly and stay relevant?
3. **Require supporting evidence.** The AI selects words from the transcript. Our app checks the references and retrieves the original text and audio times.
4. **Calculate the score using fixed rules.** The AI chooses performance levels; backend code calculates the number.

**Suggested visual:**

Recording + slides → AI assessment → Evidence checks → Score + supporting audio

**Main contribution:** “We connect AI assessments to specific speech evidence through a defined scoring and checking process.”

---

**Slide 2 — How we check the scoring process**

**Goal:** Handle unsupported results without giving users misleading scores.

Show examples covered by your existing automated tests:

| Test case | Expected behavior |
|---|---|
| AI uses speech from the wrong slide | Reject that slide’s assessment |
| There is not enough evidence to assess performance | Show “insufficient evidence,” without assigning a low score |
| One slide has invalid evidence | Keep valid slide scores and withhold the overall score |
| The same performance levels are selected | Calculate the same numerical score |

**Explain the design choice:** A missing score and a poor score mean different things. The app keeps that distinction visible.

**Next validation:** Ask people to review whether the cited speech supports the advice and whether the scores match their judgments.

**What to say aloud:** “Our automated tests check evidence handling and score calculation. Human evaluation will check the accuracy and usefulness of the AI’s judgments.”

what do you think about this idea as the slide for technical depth
```

````text
{"summary":null,"strengths":[],"weaknesses":[],"improvements":[],"improvement_shortage":null}
````

#### Initial request — verbatim

```text
I've noticed that although slides are assesed their scores and feedback dont appear until every score is assessed, could we save those scores and show the ratings of eachslide as they come?
```

#### Planning follow-ups — verbatim, in order

```text
what would be the difference
```

```text
I was thinking giving just the feedback first to the user so they have something to do while waiting for ai response, score number doesnt necessarily have to be there
```

Interactive planning selection — verbatim:

```text
Show suggestions directly (Recommended)
```

#### Implementation request and approved plan — verbatim

```text
PLEASE IMPLEMENT THIS PLAN:
# Show slide feedback while scores load

## Summary

Display each slide’s saved suggestions as soon as its feedback finishes. Numeric scores continue loading separately. Reuse the existing feedback jobs, storage and polling without adding AI requests.

## Changes

- **Full Review:** Add a “Slide feedback” section above the score details and transcript. Show feedback availability as “X of Y recorded slides.”
- For each ready slide, show its highest-priority verified observation and actionable suggestion, plus “Review slide” linking to its existing review screen. Keep slides in deck order.
- **Individual Review:** Show that suggestion directly beneath the existing compact feedback rows. Keep the full-feedback dialog available.
- Allow long suggestions to wrap and scroll within the space above the fixed Full Review button. Preserve timing controls, playback and navigation; scrolling feedback must not trigger page navigation.
- Keep suggestions visible after scores arrive or grading fails. Pending scores retain their loading indicator.

## States and interfaces

- Use existing current, validated feedback from `useRunFeedbackStatus`; public APIs, stored schemas and scoring remain unchanged.
- Show verified partial feedback with its partial warning. Completed feedback with no findings says “No issue flagged”; unfinished, failed and insufficient-evidence slides retain their existing status and recovery controls.
- Preserve source and revision checks so replaced recordings or outdated feedback cannot supply current suggestions.
- Refresh through existing polling without moving focus or automatically opening feedback.

## Verification

- Exercise one completed slide while another slide and scoring remain pending; confirm the next suggestion appears without navigation.
- Confirm saved feedback survives grading failure, offline reopening and refresh failure.
- Cover partial/empty feedback, changed recordings, stale results and long English/Korean suggestions.
- Verify opening or refreshing feedback adds no generation requests.
- Run mobile `npm run check` and `npm run bundle:android`, then inspect both screens on Android with controlled feedback states.
- Record the prompts, changes and actual verification in the active Iteration 2 collaboration log.

## Assumptions

Use the v8 mobile baseline (`cdb8055`), preserving unrelated checkout edits and ongoing backend repairs. Existing worker scheduling stays unchanged: feedback appears immediately when available, but may not always finish before scoring.
```

## Environment key lookup — October 23, 2026

**Contributor:** Jooyoung · **Tool:** OpenAI Codex · **Model:** GPT-6 Luna (confirmed by Jooyoung)

```text
[Pasted text: api-1 | UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode characters in position 6…]
```

- **Result:** Reviewed the pasted API log and traced the failure to `POST /api/decks/` in `rehearsals.services.storage.store_deck`, while saving `Slide.extracted_text` from PDF extraction. The extracted text contains unpaired UTF-16 surrogate characters, which PostgreSQL/psycopg cannot encode as UTF-8; Django then also fails while rendering its debug 500 page. Existing GET requests and Celery tasks continued successfully. No source change was made; immediate workaround is to upload a PDF without malformed embedded text or sanitize extracted text before saving. No tests were run.

Follow-up prompt:

```text
does it count as a bug? the whole app was laggy because of  it i think
```

- **Result:** Classified the behavior as a backend robustness bug: malformed PDF text should be sanitized or rejected with a controlled 4xx response, rather than causing a database encoding exception and Django's secondary 500-rendering exception. The pasted log supports the failed upload and server error; it does not by itself prove that every UI lag symptom came from this request. No source change or performance test was performed.

Follow-up prompt:

```text
Each team member should personally use the app, run manual test cases and record what they observed.
For example, a member could test importing slides, recording, playback and retaking a recording. For each case, they should record:
- Their name, test date, device and app version.

- Actual behavior and whether the case passed or failed.
- A screenshot or video timestamp supporting the result.
We can divide cases among members using a shared checklist. My recommendation is that everyone tries the core rehearsal flow, then divides the remaining edge cases.
This describes responsibility for future testing; existing test records keep their actual testers and results.
```

- **Manual test record:** Jooyoung’s October 23 write-up identifies a Galaxy Tab S7 FE and labels the app version “PR #31.” Steps were to open the app, upload the malformed PDF, observe around 07:14 and retry or observe the response. Expected behavior was successful upload or a controlled validation error while the rest of the app stayed responsive; the test failed after two HTTP 500 responses. Follow-up prompt:

```text
i uploaded the "malformed" pdf around 7:14. write up
```

- **Incident write-up:** The supplied log contains successful review, audience-Q&A and presentation-score GET requests immediately before the upload. At the log's 22:14:27 and 22:14:40 timestamps, repeated `POST /api/decks/` requests entered `rehearsals.views.decks` and `rehearsals.services.storage.store_deck`, then failed while saving `Slide.extracted_text`. Psycopg raised `UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode characters ... surrogates not allowed`, followed by Django's debug 500 response renderer raising the same error. The requests ended as HTTP 500 responses. The log therefore confirms a repeatable malformed-PDF upload failure around the reported 7:14 local time (the container/Django timestamps are shown in a different timezone); it does not identify whether an emoji caused the malformed text or independently prove app-wide lag. No source change was made.


Each request also prints the error several times because the original database encoding failure triggers a second failure while Django renders the debug error page. An earlier supplied log showed the same failure pattern at 21:03:34.

These remain manual observations; the log confirms repeated backend failures but does not independently establish causation for every lag or UI symptom. No source change was made.
